correctness.rationale: The starting density formula is explicitly credited to Britton et al.: mu_{n,t}=E[g_{min(T_n,t)}], pi_n=E[g_{T_n}], with T_n Gamma(shape n, rate r) and g_v Gaussian of variance 2Dv. After scaling to U_n= r T_n/n, the difference is E[1_{U_n>c}(g_c-g_{U_n})]. Dividing by the positive g_c leaves a strictly decreasing function of |x|, since for U_n>c the ratio g_{U_n}/g_c is strictly increasing in x^2; at zero the difference is positive and as |x| grows negative, proving exactly one positive crossing. Gamma LLN gives L1 convergence of variance mixtures to normal densities and the explicit theta<1 TV formula, while Gamma Chernoff controls theta>1. In the n+s sqrt(n) critical window, Gamma CLT and bounded second moments give sqrt(n) E(U_n-c)_+ -> phi(s)-s(1-Phi(s)); uniform L1 Taylor control of Gaussian variance derivatives yields limiting signed density -[...]*g_1' and TV coefficient (1/2)||g_1'||_1=phi(1). Independent finite numerical Gamma-mixture quadrature found the unique crossings and profile convergence at n=4,16,64, supporting but not replacing these limits.

value.rationale: The model has published stationary and transient tagged-particle distributions but the global total-variation approach is a natural strong distributional relaxation statistic not equivalent to local accumulation time. The theorem distinguishes a non-cutoff macroscopic profile from a vanishing Gaussian critical layer with exact coefficient, a useful refinement for a canonical nested reset chain.

final_claim: For tagged particle n of the equal-rate Brownian nested resetting chain from zero, the finite-time/stationary difference of position densities has a unique positive crossing. At t=theta n/r the total-variation distance tends to the explicit normal-density TV profile for theta<1 and zero for theta>=1, with a Chernoff bound for theta>1. At t=(n+s sqrt(n))/r, sqrt(n) times TV tends to phi(1)[phi(s)-s(1-Phi(s))].
limitations: Tagged marginal only; all coordinates start at zero, same r,D>0.
Asymptotic scaling not an ordinary sharp cutoff and not uniform in all theta,s.
